_provenance: HAND-AUTHORED field-note ledger — the THIRD evidence leg beside the DATA ledger (book/data/data-claims.json) and the LITERATURE positioning (book-models/lit-positioning.json). A field note is a lived DocAble incident narrated in the book that can BACK a reality-claim: not a measured datum and not an outside citation, but first-hand engineering experience. substantiation.py reads this at query time (rule-#33 best form) as `FieldNoteBacking`, symmetric with DataBacking / LiteratureBacking. Each entry: {id, incident, chapter_slug, backs_claims: [claim-id...], limitation}. A note binds to a claim (a SPINE claim, a THEORY node, or a DISCUSSION claim id) by listing the claim id in `backs_claims`. A note carrying a stated `limitation` is honest evidence — a lived observation with its bounds named, the same honesty shape a preliminary datum-with-limitation has.
_note: BINDING WAVE (harvest 260805): the two originally-seeded incidents now carry their claim bindings, and the field-note leg gains the harvest's approved evidence — I1 (measurement honesty / discriminative headroom), E1 (Definition-of-Done drift-catch efficacy), I-D (the MMM real-bug ledger), plus the two MFN-3 Epic-dir notes registered here by content (mbse-powered fuzzing technique; the MMM DRY-opportunity detector). Each carries its stated limitation verbatim from the harvest packet — a null located-not-measured, a catch-rate over snapshotted classes, a find-rate with LOW-severity caveats, a module-granularity census, a not-yet-formalized lens. The parent-repo promotion of the two MFN-3 notes into docs/field-notes/ is a SEPARATE step (not this ledger's); this ledger registers their CONTENT as book-side FieldNoteBacking so the substantiation model can cite them.

field_notes.incident: A worktree-cleanup guard failed three times in five days, each time destroying a live agent's work — the recurring failure that motivated converting the ad-hoc cleanup into a guarded, id-aware mechanism.
field_notes.limitation: Single operator, single repository; the frequency is one project's experience, not a measured rate.

field_notes.incident: An entire front end was moved to a typed language over a weekend with no observed defects — the lived instance behind the refactoring-is-cheap-under-a-strong-environment claim.
field_notes.limitation: One migration, no controlled comparison; 'no defects observed' is bounded by what the environment's gates could see.

field_notes.incident: A per-task MBSE ablation returned a null that was an ARTIFACT of zero discriminative headroom — both arms scored at ceiling (nav 40/40; impl 119/124), so the instrument could not have detected an assist if one existed. The lesson: a task small enough to freeze into a benchmark cell was small enough to solve without the map; MBSE's value is SYSTEM-level (fix-once-benefits-all, drift/parity over time, a context-bounded fleet operating a context-exceeding codebase), which no single gate-pass cell can measure.
field_notes.limitation: The per-task instrument could not discriminate (both arms at ceiling), so the system-level value is LOCATED, not measured — a null from a non-discriminating instrument is uninformative, neither for nor against the hypothesis. The note itself corrects the record, retracting a prior 'measured null' claim.

field_notes.incident: A measured efficacy refresh of the Final-Opus Definition-of-Done drift-catch: across N=36 (through 07-28) plus N=20 (07-29..08-03) closed Epics, the catch-rate for model<->code drift under a fixed drift-type taxonomy (STALE-HEADER / SECTION-4-PHASE-NOTE-GAP / STALE-TEST / TRACEABILITY-BROKEN / DOC-CLAIM / NO-DOC-SURFACE). The thesis it grounds: derived defends; snapshotted drifts.
field_notes.limitation: The catch-rate is measured over the SNAPSHOTTED drift classes in the fixed taxonomy only; the structural class the Definition-of-Done alone cannot catch is its stated limitation. Single operator, single repository, a bounded corpus of closed Epics — an efficacy reading, not a controlled comparison.

field_notes.incident: Across six model-Epics, model-based reasoning surfaced FOUR confirmed real product defects (a mislabeled CLI exit-code seam, a chunk-leak on the content-fail cleanup path, an unfenced editor lost-update race, a monotonic-drift queue-depth counter) — the signal Epics all found something actionable; the clean Epics each produced an architectural strengthening move instead. The 'modeling catches real bugs' evidence.
field_notes.limitation: Four defects over six efforts, TWO of the four LOW-severity; a find-rate over one product's window, single operator, single fleet — a lived find-rate, not a controlled defect-yield comparison.

field_notes.incident: The architecture model was made the single source of truth for BOTH halves of a fuzzing program: the fuzz-target census (derived from the model's boundary edges, invariants, external seams, and output contracts) AND the correctness oracle (derived from the model's invariants and must-never-be-read-as contracts), with coverage a bidirectional lint. It caught a real zip-bomb (a 957 KiB upload forcing ~327 MB of decompress), a never-raise-contract breach on a malformed ZIP central directory, and four latent element-granularity crashes in a JSON struct-tree parser; the model-indexed invariant campaign then ran clean (proof-shaped) over the LINEAR subset.
field_notes.limitation: The derived census is module-granularity, and the auto-oracle qualifies ONLY for LINEAR / single-call invariants with a runtime enforcement site and a total observable predicate; concurrency-safety and liveness stay in the exhaustive-BFS / TLC tier (input-fuzzing is the wrong checker there). Registered here by content from the Epic-dir note; the parent-repo promotion into docs/field-notes/ is a separate step.

field_notes.incident: The model<->code link graph the Missing-Model-Metric populates is invertible: read backwards it surfaces same-action / different-model-node consolidation candidates, duplicated shared-vocabulary across a boundary (the C#/Python CLI exit-code drift was a confirmed hit), and incomplete-composition (which cleanup-class paths reach the CANONICAL seam vs a partial sibling — which fired twice and caught a real chunk-leak bug). The traceability graph earns a SECOND keep: a lens for accidental complexity, not only for un-governed code.
field_notes.limitation: Still a field note by A.24 (trigger on the trait, not the mere possibility): fired on three of six model Epics, not yet a formalized query surface — floated as the larger scheme, deliberately not built until the yield stabilizes. Registered here by content from the Epic-dir note; the parent-repo promotion into docs/field-notes/ is a separate step.

field_notes.incident: A remediation pass-pipeline that was genuinely clean — one driver, one phase taxonomy, one typed pass-metadata contract, a topological sort validating pass order at type-init — had nonetheless drifted at seven sites where the declared order no longer matched what actually executed. The accidental divergences were not scattered: they clustered exactly where the accessibility-GenAI remediation loop iterated hardest (the PowerPoint and PDF runners), because each new generation bet was wired inline 'for now' outside the pass registry, and the one in-code guard — the topo-sort — quantified only over REGISTERED passes, so every inline addition was invisible to it. The formats carrying little GenAI surface (the spreadsheet and document runners) stayed clean. The lesson: an open loop — an iteratively capability-adding subsystem — with neither a constraint that forbids the wrong shape nor a sensor that makes drift visible will decay a clean architecture, and it decays fastest exactly where iteration is most active. The fix pairs re-absorbing the inline work into the model with a live-parity sensor that compares the passes actually executed against the declared graph.
field_notes.limitation: One pipeline in one product, single operator; the seven-site drift count and its concentration where iteration is hottest are one project's lived observation, not a measured rate across systems. The distinction the note leans on — corrosion (accidental inline drift a sensor must catch) versus library-forced essential divergence (correctly allowlisted) — is a judgment call, not a mechanical signal.

field_notes.incident: A multi-chunk document job hung for nearly an hour on staging — never completing, never failing — because the newer serverless fan-out published each chunk in a non-atomic per-chunk loop, and a created-but-undelivered task stranded the remaining chunks with no exception raised. Two model invariants formally declared this state impossible, but their satisfaction anchor covered only the older enqueue plane; a second backend had been added without re-anchoring them, so the new loop was invisible to the model. The exhaustive-state check compounded the blindness by stubbing the publish step (one chunk, always delivered), leaving the lost-subset state structurally unreachable in its search — a strong but static model suite that could never surface the class. It was found live, under load, by a warm-performance sweep, not by any single-call test; the fix re-anchored both invariants to the new plane, made the publish re-drivable, added a completeness sweep, and de-stubbed the search so the bug became reachable and a witness could go red then green.
field_notes.limitation: One incident in one product; a lived find under a specific staging load, not a measured detection rate. The two lessons it grounds — a satisfaction anchor that covers one plane while the code runs two, and a stubbed validation step that makes an invariant unfalsifiable — are cautions on WHEN a model's defense holds, not evidence that modeling generally fails; the note is the honest limit-case of the 'modeling catches real bugs' record.

field_notes.incident: A worktree-reap fix landed with fifteen green unit pins and a clean self-report, and it did not work: every run still reaped nothing, and the operator kept force-cleaning landed worktrees by hand for the rest of the session. The pins exercised the reap wrapper in isolation — they built the completion marker themselves and asserted the wrapper's return value — while the real defect lived one layer down, in a second guard INSIDE the subprocess the wrapper shells out to. A green unit suite over the unit-in-isolation is silent about the seam the unit crosses. The remedy was one honest end-to-end pin that drives the real land-then-clean path, faking only the leaf subprocesses with a faithful contract; it goes red on the bug and green with the fix. The operator's own repeated manual toil was the ground-truth signal that 'passed its pins' did not mean 'works' — operator friction is a symptom worth root-causing, not just working around.
field_notes.limitation: A single incident, single operator; illustrative of a seam-blindness class rather than a measured miss-rate. 'Prefer one end-to-end seam pin over N isolated-unit pins' holds for behavior whose value is an integration outcome; it is not a claim that unit pins are generally inferior.
